name: Mawa Kachori
subtitle: jodhpur's sweet kachori — khoya and nuts in flaky pastry, drowned in syrup

ingredients.qty: 60ml for the dough, plus 700ml for frying

ingredients.note: the filling — use fresh, crumbly khoya if you can get it

ingredients.qty: 100g, powdered for the filling, plus 350g for the syrup
175ml for the syrup, plus about 100ml for the dough

ingredients.note: half in the filling, half to garnish

prepNotes: Roast the grated khoya and cool it completely before filling — warm khoya melts, runs and bursts the pastry in the oil.
Rub the ghee into the flour until a squeezed fistful holds together. This is what makes the crust flaky rather than hard.
Have the syrup made and just warm. Kachoris are dipped hot from the fryer.

steps.text: Rub the 60ml ghee into the maida with the pinch of salt for 3 minutes, then add water gradually to a soft dough. Cover and rest 30 minutes.
Roast the grated khoya in a dry pan over low heat 6-8 minutes until it smells nutty and turns pale gold. Spread on a plate and cool fully.
steps.tip: Cool means cold. This is the step people skip and then wonder why the kachoris leak.

steps.text: Mix the cold khoya with the powdered sugar, cardamom, almonds, cashew, half the pistachios, raisins and dried coconut.
Boil the 350g sugar with 175ml water 6 minutes to a one-string syrup, add the saffron, and keep it warm.
Divide the dough into 8. Roll each into a 9cm disc, thicker in the middle than at the rim.
Place a heaped tablespoon of filling in the centre, gather the edges up over it, pinch tightly shut and twist off the excess dough.
steps.tip: Any gap in the seal and the filling escapes into the ghee — pinch hard and check each one.

steps.text: Flatten each gently with your palm into a 7cm disc and rest them seam-down for 10 minutes.
Heat the frying ghee to a low 140C — a kachori should take a good 10 seconds to float up.
Fry 4 at a time for 12-14 minutes on low, spooning ghee over them, until blistered and pale gold all over.
steps.tip: If they brown in under 8 minutes the ghee is too hot and the pastry inside stays raw.

steps.text: Drain briefly, then dip each hot kachori in the warm syrup for 30 seconds and lift onto a plate.
Crack open the top, spoon a little extra syrup inside, scatter the remaining pistachios and serve warm.

storage: Best the day they are made. Keeps 2 days at room temperature, syrup kept separate; warm 6 minutes in a 170C oven and dip again before serving.

nutrition.method: Estimated from raw ingredients using USDA FoodData Central. Cooking losses are not modelled and added salt is excluded, so sodium is not given.
nutrition.caveat: Much of the weighed input may not be eaten — syrup left in the bowl, or batter that yields more than the stated servings.
